2. State technical/design decisions and assumptions.
3. Provide most likely effort for each activity in work-hours.
4. Calculate total.

Activities:
- U1: RxJava module implementation (Design, implement, test) -> 24h
- U2: ACL Spike (Research, design, document) -> 16h
- U3: CPU Startup Spike (Profiling, analysis, documentation) -> 16h
- U4/U5: HDFS uber-jar storage (Implement HDFS storage and retrieval, HA integration) -> 32h
- U6: Override HDFS location (Configuration properties, integration) -> 8h
- U7: Override YARN config location (Configuration properties, integration) -> 8h
- U8: Stop existing Spark job (Implement stop command, resource cleanup) -> 16h
- Integration & System Testing -> 16h
- Documentation -> 8h

Total: 24 + 16 + 16 + 32 + 8 + 8 + 16 + 16 + 8 = 144 hours.

Technical and design decisions:
- Use Spring Framework 6.0+ with Java 17.
- RxJava integration will follow standard Spring module patterns.
- HDFS integration will use standard Hadoop client libraries.
- Configuration overrides will be handled via Spring Environment properties.
- Spark job management will use SparkLauncher or REST API.

Assumptions:

- The developer has access to the existing codebase and necessary Hadoop/YARN/Spark environments.
- Unit and integration tests are included in the implementation activities.
- The "CF user" refers to a Cloud Foundry user or a specific configuration role, and overrides are done via standard Spring configuration mechanisms.

technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Framework 6.0+ with Java 17 as the baseline.
Implement the RxJava module as a standard Spring processor component.
Use standard Hadoop client libraries for HDFS integration and HA features.
Implement configuration overrides (HDFS and YARN locations) using Spring Environment properties and @ConfigurationProperties.
Manage Spark jobs using SparkLauncher or the Spark REST API to enable stopping jobs and cleaning up resources.
assumptions: User stories U4 and U5 are identical and will be implemented as a single feature to avoid duplicate work.
The developer has access to the existing codebase, CI/CD pipeline, and necessary Hadoop/YARN/Spark test environments.
Unit and integration testing are included within the respective feature implementation activities.
The 'CF user' refers to a Cloud Foundry user or a configuration role, and overrides are handled via standard Spring configuration mechanisms.
The spikes (U2 and U3) will result in documentation and design specs, not production-ready code.

activities.activity_description: Design, implement, and test the flexible RxJava module to act as a processor within the Spring application.
Review customer use cases, identify the best approach for XD runtime, define DSL and UI scope, and document next steps and phases for ACLs.
Profile admin and container servers to identify high CPU startup bottlenecks, document reasons, and list pros/cons of potential solutions.
Implement the ability to store and retrieve the custom module uber-jar in HDFS, leveraging HDFS HA features for reliable reads and reinstalls under failure scenarios.
Implement configuration overrides allowing users to change the HDFS location where the custom module uber-jar is stored and retrieved.
Implement configuration overrides allowing users to change the YARN config location for custom module uber-jar storage and retrieval.
Implement the functionality to stop an existing Spark job to clean up resources at the time of completion.
Perform end-to-end integration testing of all implemented features (RxJava, HDFS, YARN, Spark) to ensure they work together correctly.
Update user and developer documentation to reflect the new RxJava module, HDFS/YARN configurations, and Spark job management features.
